title: Drowning
html_source: VANCOUVER — The first thing a visitor learns about deep diver Phil Nuytten is that he thinks big…He scoffs at fear of the deep and says the reason is because he “drowned” at the age of 18…He decided to do the 30-metre section three times, one more than the other guy. But on the last leg, on the verge of blacking out, he realized the safety diver wasn’t there…“My lungs were on fire. Finally, I exhaled all the air and immediately sucked in water. It went all the way down to my stomach,” he says…He survived when a diver noticed his absence and quickly jumped down with a fresh tank. On the boat, water was poured out of his lungs… The feeling was incredible, but in a good way. “There is a great fear that drowning is a terrible way to go. It’s not that way at all. It was kind of pleasant … I tell people I only suffered partial brain damage,” he deadpans.
